title: Requirements and the project tree
description: The Desktop CNC Mill's requirements in OpenV: the table and the tree, a requirement with its reference, attributes and links, and the wording check.

steps.say: This is the Desktop CNC Mill, a sample product in OpenV. Its requirements, user needs, hazards, design items and tests all live in one project.
The line along the top counts them: how many are traced, how many are verified, and how many have a wording problem.
Open a user need, and the panel on the right shows its text, its reference, and every requirement that derives from it.
This requirement says how accurately the mill must position the tool. Its reference, R E Q two, stays the same however often the text changes.
Further down are its links: the need it comes from, the test that verifies it, and six requirements in the frame, motion and control projects that refine it.

do: text=From a file to cutting without a sp
steps.say: The coloured score is the wording check. It reads each requirement against the shall convention and marks weak words and anything that cannot be tested.
Switch to the tree to see the same project as an outline, heading by heading.
Everything here is versioned, so you can see what each requirement said at any point, and compare two baselines of the whole project.
